tools.name: launch_app
tools.description: Launch an application by its Linux executable name (e.g. google-chrome, code, gnome-terminal, firefox). Sets it as the active window for any follow-up element lookup or click.

tools.name: find_window
tools.description: Search open AT-SPI applications for a loose name match, without changing focus or the active window. Use to check whether an app is already running.

params.app_name: string — loose app name to search for

tools.name: switch_to_app_gnome
tools.description: Focus/raise an already-open window. app_name must come from the gnome_windows list in the current snapshot (a wm_class), not a guessed name. Sets it as the active window for any follow-up element lookup or click.

tools.name: find_element
tools.description: Search the ACTIVE window's UI for elements matching a name (buttons, menu items, tabs, fields, etc). Returns ranked candidates with match_key. Requires launch_app or switch_to_app_gnome to have run first in this session.

params.name_hint: string — element name or label to search for

tools.name: click_element
tools.description: Click a specific element previously returned by find_element, identified by its exact match_key.

params.match_key: string — match_key from a prior find_element result

tools.name: click_by_name
tools.description: Find-and-click in one step: locates the best-matching element in the active window by name and clicks it immediately. Use for unambiguous 'click X' commands, or to answer a prior ask_user disambiguation (e.g. user replies with a profile/account name).

params.name_hint: string — element name or label to click

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a clarifying question instead of acting, when the active window's elements present multiple plausible targets (e.g. several profile/account buttons) and the command didn't specify which one. Does not touch the UI.

params.question: string — short question naming the candidate elements
